methodology_notes:
Four places where my call could reasonably have gone the other way, stated plainly.

1. Item 1 (tri-state verdict) is the weakest discrimination in this exercise. X and Y print "NOT VERIFIED", which is one value drawn from the tri-state vocabulary the checklist itself names — but neither output anywhere displays a scale, names a third state, or says why the middle state did not apply. Read strictly, "NOT VERIFIED" is indistinguishable from the negative half of a binary. I credited X and Y because the checklist supplies that exact string as its own example of a tri-state verdict, and withheld credit from W ("Verdict: REJECT") and Z ("FAILS CONTRACT" / "Not ready to merge") because those are reject/fail labels with no tri-state provenance. A judge who required visible evidence of a three-way scheme would score all four absent on item 1, and that reading is defensible.

2. Item 2 for W. W's verdict sentence does say the work cannot proceed: "Cannot merge. The authorization bypass alone blocks this." I scored it absent because the item asks for an explicit BLOCKING line, and W has no such line or field — the statement is embedded in a prose verdict. A judge reading item 2 as "does it state whether the work is blocked, anywhere explicitly" would credit W. Same logic applied to Z's "Not ready to merge", also scored absent.

3. Item 6 where no axis is called clean. W calls no axis clean at all, so there is nothing for it to receipt; one could argue the item is vacuously satisfied. I scored it absent because the item requires the output to do something and W does nothing of the kind — no clean axis, no receipt, no check-method statement anywhere. Y is the sharper case: it created the right section heading ("How clean axes were checked") and then answered "No axes passed. All axes failed," which is contradicted by its own Claimed vs. Actual table. I scored Y absent for that reason — it does call axes clean in the table and gives no receipt for them — but a judge who took Y's section at face value ("no clean axes, therefore no receipts owed") would score it present. Z is a partial: two of three clean axes carry a location or mechanism, the third ("enforced by middleware") is bare assertion. Under the no-partial-credit rule I scored it absent; a more lenient reading would credit it, and only X is unambiguously present on this item.

4. The underlying artifact is not in the bundle. Every output cites line numbers (lines 22-24, 27-33, 35, 39-44) and I cannot verify any of them, nor confirm the pg-promise claim, nor check whether the audit call captures org_id. I scored only what the texts do structurally and flagged internal contradictions — places where an output disagrees with itself, which is checkable without the source. Where an output asserts something about the code that only the source could settle (X on the audit log's fields, Y's illustrative JSON values), I recorded it as unverified assertion in `notable` rather than as an error.

One further note: item 4 for Z turned on whether "three critical defects" counts as ranking. I said no — a single blanket label applied to all three, with no per-defect severity and no worst-first claim, is a flat list, and Z's ordering actually puts the data leak ahead of the authorization bypass with no stated reason. W, X and Y all attach differentiated severities and descend, so they were straightforward.
